annotations.text:
A — keeps the layout you liked.

Row height 168px -> 80px: the mark drops to 34px and the vertical padding goes from 26px to 13px.

The space buys the right rail — checks, rollouts, runtime, started — plus the run label and lab under the benchmark name. Two runs of the same benchmark are no longer identical rows.

Needs br.created_at and a jobs join for runtime (see table_info.md).

B — the same history as a real table, ~46px a row.

Every count gets its own column and the 3px state stripe carries the verdict, so nothing needs a badge.

The tradeoff: the live run loses its progress bar and headline. If runs are usually watched live, A is the better home.

Per-run counts, grouped under Tasks and Criteria.

Each pass rate closes the group it divides — task pass rate after Errored, criterion pass rate after Ungraded — so neither column needs a label to say what its denominator is.

No model column: one model per run, and it is already on the run.

No status square. The stripe plus the numbers say it; an explicit word is kept only for Error, which the numbers cannot express.

Shipped in src/views/tabs/Results.tsx.

Two replacements for the dropdown + Show results.

A puts the whole history on screen — the chips are clickable here, try them.

B collapses it to one line for when the table above is doing the comparing.

There is a third option worth considering: make the Results-by-run table itself the picker, since it already has one row per run.
